ledger.claim: The recorded trace places this trip at 34.17 km against a booked optimal of 27.1 km — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of the optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are therefore passed (the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED and the case cannot be disposed of as NO_ACTION on the rider's own trip evidence.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement of actual distance, and that field reads 34.17 km on EV-GPS-00104. The trip_record.actual_distance_km of 34.2 km is the rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test, so the threshold finding rests on the trace figure and is safe.

The driver's second excuse — the CTE breakdown advisory — cannot reduce the excess at all, and I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. Its own payload records intersects_route false on a CTE corridor the trace never enters, and POL-RD-03 provides that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing.

The chat log does not convert this into a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. The only rider message in the thread is 'ok but not too long ah'; the rider names no road and no place, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the clause's corroboration test cannot be run and the diversion is not excluded from excess on that ground.

Even on the driver's best case — that the PIE accident advisory at EV-ADVIS-00104-01 exonerates part of the diversion — POL-RD-03 caps that exoneration at min(measured excess 7.07 km, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 30.1 km - booked optimal 27.1 km) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. The vehicle was driven 34.2 km, roughly 4.1 km beyond even the shortest lawful alternative, so at least 2.17 km of this trip's excess is unjustified and falls to be refunded.

Running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x surge_multiplier 1.0 (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Against charged_total of 43.41 the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60, which is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount and not a de minimis NO_ACTION (it exceeds the SGD 0.50 floor and does not reach the 90% full-refund share).

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the artifacts: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the matching trip identifier TRP-00104, and the excess passes the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's profile does not impose any extra corroboration requirement, because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift (which needs 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not apply.

The fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider still carries the whole SGD 43.41 and the present state has not moved in the rider's favour. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling would leave that charge standing, which is why the rider asks for the partial refund identified above rather than the status quo.

The trip's own evidence establishes an external-cause exoneration under POL-RD-03. The LTA DataMall accident advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit - the very road the booked optimal route uses, the routing snapshot recording 'PIE westbound throughout' (EV-TRIP-00104). Its validity window of 20:02-21:35 on the trip date brackets the trip window 20:35:10-21:22:10, well inside the 15-minute buffer at each end, and its geometry intersects the route and overlaps the trip window. The unimpaired GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104: 283 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) shows the vehicle quitting the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 - named road the optimal traverses, window overlapping the segment, leave-and-rejoin matched by the actual route - are satisfied.

Exoneration is capped, and the cap is what answers the rider's $14 claim. On the governing trace distance (34.17 km, EV-GPS-00104) the measured excess over the booked optimal of 27.1 km is 7.07 km. The justified excess is the lesser of that figure and 130% of the additional distance of the shortest lawful alternative plus 1.0 km tolerance: min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, which is the justified_excess_km the fare artifact records against EV-FARE-00104. So 4.90 km is excused as the accident-forced detour and only 2.17 km is even capable of being charged against the driver.

The threshold runs on the trace figure, not the rounded copy. EV-GPS-00104 records trace_distance_km of 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km - an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; the rider's '34 km' and the 34.2 km convenience copy are therefore properly measured at 34.17 km.

On the measurement rule POL-RD-01 itself lays down, no refundable deviation survives. Where POL-RD-03 applies, POL-RD-01 directs that the optimal for the threshold test is the adjusted optimal that clause produces - 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km. Measured against that baseline the residual excess is 34.17 - 32.00 = 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of 32.00 km. The establishment test requires the excess to be greater than 20% of the optimal AND greater than 0.8 km, and both must pass; the relative limb fails, so POL-RD-01's own words apply - no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION, leaving the fare as charged.

If the tribunal instead treats the capped residual as refundable, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic still caps the rider's recovery far below the $14.00 claimed. Run against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km (duration 40.1 min, the booked 34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1), the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 39.828, so the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60, exactly as EV-FARE-00104 records. That is the ceiling. The $9.00 a computation against the unadjusted 27.1 km optimal would yield is not available because POL-RD-03 requires the adjusted route, and the rider's claimed $14.00 is traceable to no artifact at all.

There is no basis for the FULL_REFUND uplift the rider would need. The deviation is not MATERIAL: 7.07 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate and 26.09% is below the 50% gate set by POL-RD-01, so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged on this trip. And even if consulted, the driver's profile shows no pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a ratio of 0.0035, far below the 0.05 threshold (EV-DPROF-00104). POL-GEN-01 confines this test to exactly those two fields; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is NOT the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names and may not be substituted for it.

ledger.claim: The rider's initial POL-RD-08 burden is met on the identifiers - trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00104 with a consistent pickup - and the burden therefore shifts to the driver, who discharges it by naming a specific artifact and clause: advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) and POL-RD-03, as that clause requires. The driver's account is corroborated contemporaneously: at 20:38:12 he told the rider 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok' and at 20:38:55 the rider replied 'ok but not too long ah' (EV-CHAT-00104), so the diversion was disclosed while it was happening and was not objected to. No POL-RD-04 rider-directed-detour limb is asserted - the rider named no road and waypoint_hint is null - but the log defeats any suggestion that the driver was concealing the route he took.

The driver's statement also mentions a CTE breakdown, and that part of the account cannot carry anything: I concede it. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED (its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, and EV-GPS-00104 contains no fix inside that box at any point) and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (operator-entered rather than DataMall-ingested); intersects_route is false. POL-RD-03 provides that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing, so that advisory is discarded on the merits, and the driver's exoneration rests solely on EV-ADVIS-00104-01.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a partial refund of SGD 3.60 to the rider, being the part of the diverted route the driver cannot answer for.

The facts. All three instruments carry trip TRP-00104, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104) is unimpaired for policy purposes — 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and no jumps — so POL-RD-07 has no work to do and no escalation is required. The governing actual distance is the trace's 34.17 km (POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and forbids citing the rounded 34.2 km trip_record copy). Against the booked optimal of 27.1 km that is an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%: both POL-RD-01 gates pass and a deviation is established.

The driver's excuse, and its cap. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the road the booked optimal route uses; its 20:02-21:35 window brackets the trip; and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 and rejoining on the AYE. All three POL-RD-03 limbs are met. The exoneration is capped at min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal is 32.00 km over 40.1 minutes, and only the 2.17 km beyond the cap is charged against the driver.

The refund. Against the adjusted route the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x surge 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP or surcharge lines on this trip: 39.828. Charged total 43.41. Refund 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share.

Driver: I reject your submission that no refundable deviation survives because the residual falls under POL-RD-01's percentage gate. POL-RD-03 says in terms that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, and POL-RD-02 says in terms that where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess the computation runs against the adjusted route; reading the gate to wipe out the residual would leave both directives with nothing to operate on. Your profile is not held against you: the deviation is not MATERIAL (7.07 km against an 8.0 km gate, 26.09% against a 50% gate), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and your trailing-90-day figures (deviation_flags_90d 1 over completed_trips_90d 288) show no repeat pattern in any event.

Rider: your figure of about SGD 14.00 is not supported by any artifact. The diversion itself is excused up to the cap, and what remains is the 2.17 km residual computed above. The chat log does not convert this into a rider-requested detour: you named no road or place and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no excess is excluded on that ground — though the log does show the driver disclosing the diversion to you at 20:38:12, and your reply at 20:38:55.

The CTE advisory. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is schema-impaired at weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE; both sides correctly disclosed that and neither relies on it. It is policy-clean only in the sense of being irrelevant: its geometry covers a CTE corridor the trace never enters, so intersects_route is false, and under POL-RD-03 an advisory over a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing. Nothing in this ruling rests on it, so it does not cap confidence.

No escalation and no referral. Identifiers, timestamps and charge lines are internally consistent, the trace is unimpaired, and confidence is 0.85 against the 0.70 floor. No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises (no pattern) and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises (the fare carries no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
